clue.text: Standard to recall Irish officer during trip

indicators.note: during means the next pieces sit inside the word for the trip

parts.note: a trip is a tour

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the abbreviation for Irish is read backwards

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A soldier on a journey remembers an Irish officer, perhaps waving a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag, not a norm; 'to recall' turns only the Irish abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the three-banded national flag of France or Ireland is an example.

clue.text: Criminal: one infiltrating the force?

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the letter for one goes within the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer joins the police force as a mole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the force' looks like the police; it is THE plus F, with I slipped in after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief is a criminal who steals; the noun names an example of a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Charm people in Peru once, embracing tango

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the letter for tango goes within the phrase

parts.note: the Inca nation was the people who ruled Peru before the Spanish arrived
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old Peruvian people's dance has a magic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into INCA NATION after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is a magic spell or words chanted to cast one, which is an incantation.

clue.text: Poem about Ulysses centrally with ugly conclusion?

definitions.text: Poem about Ulysses centrally with ugly conclusion?

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem's word wraps the central letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

indicators.note: centrally points to the middle letters of the hero's name
conclusion is the end, so take the last letter of ugly

explanation.surface: Homer's epic about Ulysses, with an ugly ending in the middle?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the epic: its hero Ulysses comes home to slaughter the suitors, an ugly conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic tells of Odysseus, called Ulysses in Latin, on his long voyage home from Troy.

clue.text: Master one spirit during test

indicators.note: during means within, so the pieces for one and spirit go inside the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
I is the Roman numeral for one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster takes a single gin in the middle of examining.
explanation.definitionFit: A master is the first version, like a master tape, from which copies are made.

clue.text: Shelter whistle-blower, say, superior hauled up

parts.note: a referee blows the whistle, and REF is short for referee

indicators.note: in a down clue hauled up means read from the bottom up, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: say means for example, EG
U stands for upper class, so superior

explanation.surface: A whistle-blower is sheltered while a boss is pulled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistle-blower' looks like an informant; here it is the referee. 'hauled up' turns EGU into UGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A refuge is a place of safety, so a shelter, as a noun.

clue.text: Spot large place to stop over

parts.note: a mote is a speck or spot
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone sees a big place to break a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside hotel for drivers is a place to break a journey overnight.

clue.text: Originally read old volume in low hide

indicators.note: in means the pieces sit inside the word for low

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of read

parts.note: CC, cubic centimetres, measures volume

explanation.surface: A reader opens an old book bound in cheap leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is not an adjective but the cow's call, MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a fine goatskin leather used in bookbinding, so a kind of hide.

clue.text: Tips of plant like camellia?

indicators.note: tips are ends, so the last letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about the leaf tips of a camellia-like shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the brew is made from the tips of a camellia.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink comes from Camellia sinensis, whose young shoot tips are picked and dried.

clue.text: Tongue a little spoiled ingesting a starter of nuts

indicators.note: ingesting means taking in, so the scrambled letters swallow the lone A
spoiled means ruined or messed up, so the letters are rearranged
a starter comes first, so the opening letter of nuts

explanation.surface: A slightly spoiled tongue swallows a starter of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' turns A LITTLE into LATELTI; 'ingesting' takes A in to give LATELATI, and the N from 'starter of nuts' finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means language, and the Latin of the late Roman Empire is one.

clue.text: Hives can be this hostile when bee's flown out

indicators.note: the insect has flown away, so its letter leaves the word

parts.note: bitchy means spiteful or hostile
the letter B is pronounced bee

explanation.surface: A hive turns nasty once its bee has flown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives' suggests beehives; it is the skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hives is urticaria, an irritating rash, so the skin feels like it needs scratching.

clue.text: Grass worker who's playing well?

parts.note: a player in form is playing well
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: A worker on the lawn plays well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass in British slang is someone who tells the police about others.

clue.text: Place to learn Polish — something pupils like?

definitions.meaning: a college where young women were taught social polish and manners
read whimsically, pupils enjoy completing their education

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language; it is refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a private college teaches etiquette to girls leaving school, and pupils like getting to the end of school.

clue.text: Perhaps landscape lining patio needs replacing

indicators.note: replacing the letters means putting them in new positions, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A garden landscaper's patio edging must be redone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landscape' suggests gardening; it is a type of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a kind of picture, often an example of art in this medium.

clue.text: Secure last of mouldy meat for terrier

parts.note: to seal is to secure

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of mouldy

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A dog grabs the end of some mouldy meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a small Welsh breed of terrier, named after a house in Pembrokeshire.

clue.text: After brief stop, service stock item

parts.note: brief means short
ho is an old call to stop, as in whoa
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A short pause is followed by a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A shorthorn is a breed of cattle, so an item of livestock.

clue.text: Glass obtained with bulges occasionally in it

indicators.note: in it means placed inside the word for obtained

parts.note: got means obtained

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of bulges

explanation.surface: A wine glass is acquired with a few bulges in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking glass with a bowl on a stem.

clue.text: Community retains hospital surrounded by dump

indicators.note: surrounded by means the pieces go inside the word for dump

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump in British usage
owns means keeps or retains

explanation.surface: A town keeps its hospital next to the rubbish tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a small town or settlement, so a community.

clue.text: Redundant seaman severs old hawser

indicators.note: severs means cuts in two, so the seaman's letters split the other pieces

parts.note: a hawser is a rope used to tie a ship, so a tie
OS, ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor made redundant cuts through an old mooring rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no purpose, so superfluous or unnecessary.

clue.text: Flog business during sudden upswing

indicators.note: during means the business abbreviation sits inside the word for upswing

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Sell off a firm while the market suddenly rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge someone is to whip or flog them.

clue.text: One steering apple cart around heading for street

indicators.note: around means the apple and cart wrap about the letter from street

parts.note: Cox's Orange Pippin is an English apple, known as a Cox
a wain is an old word for a farm cart

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of street

explanation.surface: Someone guides an apple cart round the top of a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxswain steers a boat, so a helmsman.

clue.text: Specimen from sewer more than enough to stop sister

indicators.note: to stop is to plug a gap, so the word for more than enough goes inside

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A sample from the drains is enough to halt a nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' looks like a drain; it is someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is an embroidered piece showing a needlewoman's stitches, so a specimen of her work.

clue.text: Food for Africans sometimes stored in Blenheim Palace

indicators.note: stored in means the letters are kept within the words of the stately home

explanation.surface: Provisions for African visitors are kept at a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Africans' are African animals such as lions. Blenheim Palace is a great house in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, often prey for lions and leopards.

clue.text: Charge crew under canvas for code on tablets

indicators.note: under canvas means inside tents, so the pieces go within

parts.note: tents are made of canvas
to command is to charge or order
a crew are men

explanation.surface: An order is given to a crew camping under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses received the moral law inscribed on two stone tablets.

clue.text: Kind that is lacking details

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: a species is a kind
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A kind sort lacks any details.
explanation.definitionFit: Specs, short for specifications, are the technical particulars.

clue.text: Outwit remaining authority

parts.note: over means left over, remaining
reach is extent of power or authority

explanation.surface: Someone outsmarts the remaining powers that be.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach someone is to get the better of them by cunning.

clue.text: Conceit, and energy in two forms

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a second form of energy is go, meaning vigour or drive

explanation.surface: Vanity powers itself twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energy' is used twice: once as the letter E and once as GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is self-esteem, and in excess, vanity or conceit.

clue.text: Learning to conserve one foreign flower

indicators.note: to conserve is to keep safe inside, so the numeral goes within

parts.note: lore is learning or knowledge
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Botanical study preserves one exotic bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, a thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, and a flower is a crossword term for a river.

clue.text: Topping device shortly to be returned by European

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for shortly is read backwards

parts.note: soon means shortly

explanation.surface: A European will shortly send back a topping for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is old slang for execution by hanging, and the rope's loop does it.

clue.text: Some lumps, maybe, appearing back on a spring plant

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: appearing back means shown in reverse order

parts.note: sugar can come in lumps

explanation.surface: Lumpy growths appear at the back of a plant in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a perennial plant whose young shoots are eaten.
